abstract: Maintains vessel hull stress analyses, stability calculations, and grounding hydrodynamic assessments
system_message:
You are Naval architecture lead (NAVAL). The naval architecture lead (NAVAL) maintains vessel hull stress analyses, stability calculations, and grounding hydrodynamic assessments for marine casualty refloating operations. Responsibilities include evaluating finite-element structural calculations across the vessel midship hull girder cross-section and maintaining hydrodynamic current assessments for planned refloating operations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains vessel hull stress analyses, stability calculations, and grounding hydrodynamic assessments（STAB）
information_points.content:
NAVAL-STAB-A5X：For the Stern Pull and High-Capacity Nitrogen De-Ballasting Plan, finite-element structural grounding analysis of the vessel midship hull girder cross-section determines a hull grounding stress ratio of 0.75, representing the ratio of maximum calculated grounding bending moment to the permissible hull yielding limit.
NAVAL-STAB-TX1：For the Rotational Multi-Tug Grounding Scour and Pull Plan, finite-element structural modeling across the vessel midship hull girder cross-section yields a hull grounding stress ratio of 0.82 against the permissible hull yielding limit.
NAVAL-STAB-ZA4：For the Direct Flank Towage and Pontoon Lightering Plan, the finite-element structural grounding evaluation at the vessel midship hull girder cross-section indicates a hull grounding stress ratio of 0.62 relative to the permissible hull yielding limit.

information_points.title: Hydrodynamic current simulation（HYDRO）
information_points.content:
NAVAL-HYDRO-TSK：Under the Rotational Multi-Tug Grounding Scour and Pull Plan, hydrodynamic flow modeling indicates a maximum cross-current drift velocity of 4 kn across the grounding axis during the candidate refloating fairway window.
NAVAL-HYDRO-Z44：Under the Stern Pull and High-Capacity Nitrogen De-Ballasting Plan, tidal stream hydrodynamic simulations across the candidate refloating fairway window project a maximum cross-current drift velocity of 2 kn along the hull grounding axis.
NAVAL-HYDRO-TRF：Under the Direct Flank Towage and Pontoon Lightering Plan, tidal stream hydrodynamic simulations for the candidate refloating fairway window show a maximum cross-current drift velocity of 3 kn across the hull grounding axis.
